subject: Fleet capacity sizing — per-model context + KV memory & quant tradeoffs
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@greengrid.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Estimating dedicated capacity for long-context summarization

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the product demo earlier this week — Victor and I walked the team through Redwood and we're excited about a Dedicated deployment. We have two models in scope: a fine-tuned LLaMA-2-13B variant (up to 32k tokens) used for document summarization, and a distilled conversational model (open-source) for chat assistants (up to 4k tokens).

High-level ask: we need a ballpark for committed GPU capacity and an initial monthly estimate tied to our Q3 pilot (expected 5M tokens/month for summarization, 3M tokens/month for chat). Key constraints:
- Latency target for summarization tail p95 < 500ms per request
- We will enable aggressive prefix KV caching for repeated documents
- We are willing to accept quantized variants if memory reductions are meaningful and quality stays within a 3% ROUGE delta

Can you outline assumptions you need and a conservative sizing recommendation (GPU types, count, headroom for peak bursts)? Also any notes on how quantization (4-bit vs 8-bit) and per-request context length / KV cache residency will change GPU memory requirements would be helpful.

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Zhao
Director of ML Infrastructure
Greengrid Technologies

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Estimating dedicated capacity for long-context summarization

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear brief. Looping in Marissa (Account Lead) and Sean (Inference Architect) to propose a scoped sizing based on your usage profile. 

Quick notes up-front:
- We treat per-model KV cache residency separately from live per-request memory. For long-context summarization the KV cache will be the dominant driver if you keep many large documents hot.
- Quantization will reduce model weights memory significantly, but KV cache (activations/keys/values) scales with max context and batch concurrency and is less compressible; however 4-bit kernel paths plus packed KV storage give some wins.

We’ll put together a two-scenario estimate: conservative (no quantization, N-replicas for latency SLO) and optimized (mixed precision + 4-bit weights + cached KV storage). Marissa — can you confirm the procurement cadence and target start for a Dedicated reserve so we can align on committed vs burst capacity?

Next: Sean will follow with model-level numbers (estimated GPU RAM per replica at 32k / 8k / 4k contexts for the two models) and suggest GPU SKUs.

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emily — sending a short commercial note alongside the technical sketch that Sean will provide. Attached is a first-pass sizing workbook (GG-Fleet-Sizing-v1.xlsx) with line items for committed GPUs (monthly), burst credits, and optional 24/7 canary support. Highlights: 

- Conservative baseline (no quantization): 6 x A100-80GB for replication and headroom. Assumptions: 32k context, KV cache warm for ~250 large docs concurrently, moderate batching (~1.5 tokens/req). Monthly commit: 6 reserved GPUs + 2 burst; est. token cost-equivalent shown in sheet.
- Optimized (quantized + KV packing): 4 x H100-80GB with 4-bit weights, packed KV store on NVMe-backed cache for cold docs, and aggressive prefix caching. This lowers the reserved footprint but requires initial engineering to validate quality at 4-bit; we budget 10% extra for fallback capacity during rollout.

Commercial notes: we can structure a 6-month pilot commit with a mid-pilot quality review to switch rollouts between quantized and full-precision variants. Pricing rows and a proposed MA plan are in the workbook.

Next steps: Sean will post a small table with per-model memory estimates (weights, KV residency per 1k context, offsets for 4-bit vs fp16).

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@greengrid.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Estimating dedicated capacity for long-context summarization

Emily — digging into the model math below. I’ve kept numbers conservative with buffer for tail latency and cache churn.

Summary table (quick, per replica):
- LLaMA-2-13B variant (32k max context):
  - Weights: fp16 ~26GB; 8-bit quant ~13GB; 4-bit ~8GB (packed kernels + activation stitching).
  - KV cache residency per 1k tokens: ~1.6GB (keys+values + metadata) at 32k dense layout; so a single fully-warmed 32k doc ~= 51GB of KV memory (1.6GB * 32).
  - Practical note: we rarely keep entire 32k per-doc warm; typical working set is prefixes (first ~8k) + sliding window for recent tokens. For sizing, assume 4k effective warm per doc unless you commit to full-document pinning.

- Distilled chat model (4k context):
  - Weights: fp16 ~7GB; 8-bit ~3.5GB; 4-bit ~2GB.
  - KV per 1k tokens: ~0.9GB -> 4k warm doc ~= 3.6GB.

GPU recommendations (conservative vs optimized):
- Conservative (no quant): A100-80GB x6 per fleet for replication and headroom. Rationale: weights + partial KV + concurrency for 99th percentile.
- Optimized (aggressive 4-bit + KV packing + NVMe overflow): H100-80GB x4 reserved, with 2 additional H100 for burst/fallback. We rely on kernel paths that do packed 4-bit matmuls and split KV residency between GPU DRAM and fast NVMe using our KV spill layer.

Operational knobs and the effect on capacity:
- Max context length increases peak KV memory linearly. If you cap runtime context to 8k (enforced at request ingress) you reduce worst-case GPU RAM needs ~4x versus 32k worst-case.
- Batch size and concurrency: the more concurrency per-GPU, the more KV per token you need resident. For p95<500ms we recommend targeting concurrency limits (per-GPU) and using prefix caching to reduce repeated recompute.
- Quantization fallbacks: keep 1-2 full-precision replicas to handle quality regressions during rollout (these replicas cost more RAM but protect SLA).

Example sizing (based on your volumes: 5M tokens/month summarization -> ~1.6M tokens/week -> with average request 4k tokens -> ~400 requests/week, but bursty daily patterns matter):
- Pilot reserve: Optimized path: 4x H100-80GB reserved + 2 burst = handles average plus 2x peak bursts with KV spill to NVMe. Expect to add 10-15% buffer for unexpected document pinning.

Technical caveats: KV numbers vary by model architecture and our profiler will refine by +/-20%. We recommend a 2-week profiling run on a sample of your documents to measure real warm set sizes and token distribution; that's the gating input to finalize committed counts.

I've uploaded a short PDF with per-model profiles to the Drive link Marissa included (greengrid-model-profiles.pdf).

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet on a quick call — I can also run a profiling job on a 1-week sample set if you grant us access to anonymized tokens.

—Sean Gallagher
Inference Architect, Redwood Inference
